Reduce the per-square shrink from 1e-10 to 1e-13. Float rounding in the grid coordinates is about 1e-16, so neighbouring squares should still not overlap, and a little side length is recovered. The layout is unchanged, so any gain is negligible.

Add a second DP layout: an m×m grid with two merged square blocks (j1 and j2) in opposite corners, each filled recursively, with the remaining cells filled from the existing table. The best layout per n is still chosen by the DP.

Add a fast fallback for large n (above 700), where the O(n³) DP could exceed the 60-second limit. It places the squares in a plain grid of the best size, either ceil(√n) or floor(√n). The DP layout is unchanged for smaller n.

Add a plain-grid fallback for large n (above 800), so the O(n³) DP cannot hit the 60-second limit. The grid is either floor(√n) squared cells or ceil(√n) cells holding n squares, whichever has the larger sum. The DP layout for smaller n is unchanged.

The current program has no guard against large n, so the O(n²) DP could exceed the 60-second limit. I added a plain-grid fallback for n above 1500, which takes the better of k×k cells (side 1/k) and ceil(√n) cells per side. Layouts for smaller n are unchanged.

Add a guard so large n (above 2000) uses a plain grid layout instead of the O(n²) DP, which could exceed the 60-second limit. It takes the better of ceil(√n) cells per side and floor(√n) cells per side. Layouts for n ≤ 2000, including all the evaluated values, are unchanged.

I generalised the corner-block step of the DP. A b×b block (any 2 ≤ b ≤ a−1) now sits in one corner of an a×a grid and the remaining a²−b² cells are filled recursively. Before, only b = a−1 was allowed, so this adds layouts such as 5×5 with a 3×3 block. I also added a plain-grid fallback for n > 200

I generalised the corner step so a b×b block (2 ≤ b ≤ a−1) can sit in one corner of an a×a grid, with the remaining a²−b² cells filled recursively. Before, only b = a−1 was allowed. I also added a plain-grid fallback for n > 1500 to stay within the 60-second limit.

I add a plain-grid fallback for n > 1500, which takes the better of ceil(√n) cells per side and floor(√n) cells per side. This keeps the O(n²) DP inside the 60-second limit for large n. Layouts for smaller n are unchanged.
